Gusto pricing in 2026

Gusto publishes its prices: Simple is $49 a month + $6 per person, Plus is $80 + $12 per person and Premium is $180 + $22 per person, with free account setup and no contract. Gusto closed its Contractor-only plan to new customers on 1 October 2026; companies already on it keep it. At 25 people, list comes to $199 a month on Simple, $380 on Plus and $730 on Premium.

How the price is built

Gusto publishes its list prices and states free account setup. Paid add-ons it lists include Priority Support at $30 a month + $3 per person.

List cost at 100 employees, one year

  • Simple: $7,788 ($6 x 100 x 12 + $49 x 12)
  • Plus: $15,360 ($12 x 100 x 12 + $80 x 12)
  • Premium: $28,560 ($22 x 100 x 12 + $180 x 12)

Before volume discounts, add-ons or any renewal increase. Run your own headcount in the ledger.

What do the plans cost in 2026?

Simple $49 a month + $6 per person. Plus $80 + $12 per person. Premium $180 + $22 per person. Prices from Gusto's plan pages, read 24 November 2026.

Is the Contractor-only plan still available?

Not to new customers. Gusto's help centre says it closed the Contractor-only plan on 1 October 2026; companies already on it pay $35 a month plus $6 per contractor and nothing changes for them. On the standard plans, contractors cost $6, $12 or $22 per contractor per month depending on the plan.

Does Gusto charge a setup fee?

No. The pricing page states free account setup, no contracts and cancel any time.

What paid add-ons are there?

Gusto lists Priority Support at $30 a month + $3 per person. Its help centre lists a broker-integration add-on at $6 per employee per month for new Premium customers from 1 October 2026.

How does Gusto compare with Rippling?

Gusto publishes every plan price; Rippling publishes only a floor of $8 per employee per month plus a monthly base fee. The usual reason to pick Rippling is scope (IT and device management on the same platform), so get a Rippling quote for the modules you need and compare it with the Gusto plan in the ledger.
